english.title: Fail to submit statement of affairs to administrative receiver
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having been required under section 47 of the Insolvency Act 1986 to submit a statement of affairs to **(..SPECIFY RECEIVER..), the administrative receiver of **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..), without reasonable excuse failed to do so before the end of the period of 21 days beginning with **(..SPECIFY DATE ON WHICH NOTICE WAS GIVEN..), the day after that on which the prescribed notice of the requirement was given to you by that receiver
english.legislation: Contrary to section 47(4) and (6) of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and location
having been required under s47
to submit statement of affairs to administrative receiver
w/o reasonable excuse
failed to do so before end of the period of 21 days

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) Section 431 of the Insolvency Act 1986 provides that notwithstanding anything in section 127(1) of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980, an information relating to such an offence which is triable by a magistrates' court in England and Wales may be so tried if it is laid at any time within 3 years after the commission of the offence and within 12 months after the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Secretary of State (as the case may be) to justify the proceedings comes to his knowledge. Summary proceedings in Scotland for such an offence shall not be commenced after the expiration of 3 years from the commission of the offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum or a fine not exceeding one-tenth of the statutory maximum for each day on which the act or the failure continues.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
